title: Dev Bootcamp launchpad — quickstarts & pricing anchors
summary: Working notes for a short, developer-focused bootcamp product that communicates Redwood Hosted API value: fast time-to-first-call, predictable unit economics, and safe defaults for production. Contains quickstart angles for 15–60 minute wins, modular pricing language candidates, and competitor framing to test in user interviews.
audience: Developer-first GTM: growth PMs, developer marketing, developer advocates, solutions engineers
one_liner: Get your first LLM feature into a repo and running in production-like conditions within an hour — with predictable cost controls and zero infra maintenance.
value_props: First-call-to-prod in under 60 minutes: SDK, templates, and a starter prompt kit that demonstrate streaming, function-calling, and embeddings in one flow.
Predictable unit economics: clear token pricing examples, per-route budgets, and a default autoscale cap that prevents surprise bills.
Production-safe by default: built-in fallbacks, rate limits, and a verified model catalog to avoid silent regressions.
Swap-in deployability: start on Hosted API, then lift-and-shift to Dedicated or Private with the same API surface and rollout controls.
Observability that matters: token-level cost breakdown, tail-latency alerts, and prompt-set regression checks in the Console.
Developer ergonomics: language SDKs, CLI, and a single-line deploy for a sample app (React + serverless) with telemetry wired.
Opinionated defaults for production: batching, KV prefix cache, and light quantization profiles that balance cost/latency.
quickstart_angles: 15-minute 'hello world' CLI: install redwood-cli, api-key env var, run 'rw start-sample' -> shows streaming chat and token meter. Outcome: immediate gratification; emphasis on low friction.
30-minute feature add: add summarization to an existing API route. Show before/after latency and cost delta, include rollback snippet and a canary config.
60-minute integration: build a small Slack bot using Hosted API with function-calls. Walk through secrets, rate limit config, and canary rollout policy. Outcome: working app + runbook for scaling.
Embeddings fast-lane (20 min): take CSV of product copy -> embeddings -> vector search API. Show pricing per-embedding and tips for chunking to save costs.
Experiment path: try two models (cost/latency tradeoff) with one toggle. Provide a tiny harness to A/B and show Console metrics to pick winner.
Ops-forward dev path: demo the Dedicated switch — show how to pin a model version and enable autoscale policies without code changes.
Safety-first sample: configure content filters, show audit logs and KMS integration in 10 steps. Emphasize compliance readiness.
Snippet playbook for conversion: copy-paste ready micro-snippets for README, bug tracker, and first PR templates used by dev advocates.
Troubleshooting checklist: token exhaustion, cold-starts, model mismatch — 1-line fixes and Console links.
Workshop format: 45-minute instructor-led + 15-minute office hours for follow-ups; includes prebuilt repo and post-workshop checklist.
pricing_language_drafts: Price-first framing: 'Pay for what you use — token pricing with per-request latency tiers. No hidden infra fees.' Use example: 'Summarize 1k docs -> ~$0.12 per 1k tokens (preview).'
Risk-minimizing anchor: 'Start with free credits and a default monthly cap. We only bill above the cap with explicit opt-in.' Good for SMB devs.
Feature-tier framing: 'Hosted (PAYG) vs Dedicated (reserved commits) vs Private (platform + support).' Emphasize upgrade path and predictable TCO for commits.
Per-route budgets blurb: 'Set hard budgets per API key/route. When a route hits its budget, requests fail closed or degrade to a cheaper model.' Useful copy for docs and in-console tooltips.
Transparency snippet: 'Token meter and per-call breakdown available in Console and SDK logs — so you can map cost back to feature and PR.' Use in onboarding emails.
Trial-to-conversion wording: 'Free developer credits + a single PR-friendly invoice on first usage that exceeds credits. Easy to attach billing to org.'
competitive_notes: Competitor A (large infra provider): strong on ecosystem integrations, weaker on curated model catalog and inference economics. Opportunity: show cost-per-100k tokens comparisons on real workloads.
Competitor B (API-first LLM vendor): great UX for simple apps but limited options for predictive autoscale and private deployment. Position Redwood as the path from sandbox to SLA-backed deployments.
Competitor C (self-hosted runtime vendor): lower unit-cost at scale but high ops burden. Messaging: 'start hosted, scale on your terms' and offer a migration checklist.

Key rebuttals to common objections: (1) "Why not just use open-source locally?" -> ops + continuous optimization costs, plus slower feature velocity. (2) "Why not cheaper spot GPUs?" -> instability/complexity and hidden integration work.
Differentiator bullets to test: unified API across Hosted/Dedicated/Private; explicit cost controls; dev-first quickstarts with production guardrails.
Competitive experiments to run: pricing A/B of monthly cap vs per-route budgets; messaging A/B (velocity-first vs cost-first) in trial signups.
Examples to include in comparison table: latency SLOs (p50/p95), default autoscale behavior, model swapping friction, and available rollback strategies.
User quotes to validate messaging: 'We needed predictable inference costs more than raw throughput' and 'Single API reduced dev time for compliance reviews'. Plan interviews to capture these.
Short-term win: produce a one-page comparison cheat-sheet for SEs highlighting migration steps from competitor stacks to Redwood.
Long-term research: collect 20 conversion-fallout cases where teams didn't upgrade from Hosted -> Dedicated and annotate reasons (cost, security, org politics).
open_questions: What is the lowest friction upgrade path from PAYG to Dedicated that marketing can promise without engineering changes?
Which pricing cap defaults reduce sense-of-risk for SMB devs while still converting mid-market teams?
Do we A/B test language that uses absolute $ examples (easier) vs relative savings % (less believable)?
What guardrails should be default for trial orgs to avoid support escalations early?
Which competitor benchmarks (p95 latency, cost per 1M tokens) do we publish vs keep internal?
recommended_next_steps: Run 6 developer interviews using two message frames: 'instant velocity' vs 'predictable economics' and capture verbatim quotes.
Build a 1-hour workshop kit (repo + deck + instructor notes) and pilot with two DA sessions; capture conversion metrics.
Create a short video (90s) showing the 30-minute feature add flow with token-meter overlay for the pricing page.
Author a one-pager competitor cheat-sheet for SEs and Solutions Engineers; schedule a 30-min sync to review with GTM.
Prototype 'per-route budget' UI copy in Console and instrument a small experiment to measure reduced billing disputes.
Decide on default monthly cap for new orgs and bake into billing + onboarding copy; coordinate w/ finance for accounting implications.
